# Overview

An **eGFP copy-number ladder** on the SmBiT-P2A-FLAG backbone from `06_`, used as
a length series. **MDA-MB-231 only**, same background and gene set as `01_`,
`03_`, `04_` and `06_`.

The 36 nt Waldo folding-reporter linker (`GSAGSAAGSGEF`) precedes **every** eGFP
copy: after the FLAG tag, and again between each pair of fluorophores. The repeat
unit is therefore linker + eGFP = 759 nt. At the default settings:

| construct | eGFP copies | nt |
|---|---|---|
| SmBiT-P2A-FLAG | 0 | 117 |
| SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-1xeGFP | 1 | 876 |
| SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-2xeGFP | 2 | 1,635 |
| SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-3xeGFP | 3 | 2,394 |

`max_gfp_copies` and `linker_between_copies` are parameters and the output
filenames carry both, so a different ladder does not overwrite this one.

**`linker_between_copies` is kept as a parameter because the alternative is a
reasonable reading of the same design.** `TRUE` (the default) is the arrangement
above. `FALSE` places a single linker at the FLAG-eGFP junction only, after which
the eGFP copies are fused directly to one another, and each rung gains 723 nt
rather than 759. Directly fused tandem fluorophores are the folding problem the
Waldo linker was designed to relieve, which is why `TRUE` is the default; it also
dilutes GC3 slightly further (3x: 93.0% against 94.6%), so it is better on both
counts. The 0-copy rung never carries a linker under either setting, since there
is no eGFP for it to join.

Either way the rungs above 0 are an exactly uniform ladder; only the step size
differs. Section 2 asserts the uniformity rather than assuming it.

**The linker ends in an in-frame EcoRI site.** `GAATTC` encodes Glu-Phe at its
C terminus, which is how folding-reporter constructs are built, but it leaves
internal EcoRI sites in the ORF - one per linker. Section 2 counts them.

**This ladder is the mirror image of the FLAG ladder in `05_`.** The FLAG ladder
held GC3 still (1.6-1.9 points) while total GC drifted badly (7.6-9.3 points),
because it stacked a short GC-poor epitope. This one stacks a long GC3-extreme
protein, so **both** GC and GC3 are nearly fixed above 1 copy - the construct is
asymptotically just eGFP - but they are fixed at the wrong value. Section 6
reports both drifts rather than asserting one and ignoring the other.

**The composition problem does not improve with more copies; it gets worse.** At
1 copy the construct is GC3 93.2%, already the 99.7th percentile of the expressed
transcriptome. Every further copy pushes it toward eGFP's own 96.7%. So this is a
clean length series *only* if the experiment can tolerate running along the far
GC3 tail for its whole range. If GC3 is a variable of interest rather than a
nuisance, a codon-shuffled eGFP is the version to build - the same recoding
machinery `64_` used for NanoLuc - and this notebook is the baseline it would be
compared against.

**Tandem identical repeats are a real construction risk.** 2x and 3x carry 723 nt
and 1,446 nt of exactly repeated sequence, which recombines in *E. coli* and is
hard to sequence through. Section 3 reports the longest exact repeat per
construct. The standard fix is to use codon-divergent eGFP copies, which would
also let each copy's GC3 be chosen independently.

# Load Libraries

```{r load_libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38)
library(Biostrings)

source(here("code", "cds_reporter_design", "reporter_helpers.R"))
```

```{r params_chunk}
lfc_cutoff  <- 0.5
padj_cutoff <- 0.05

gfp_copies <- 0:params$max_gfp_copies
ladder_tag <- paste0("upto", params$max_gfp_copies, "x",
                     if (params$linker_between_copies) "_linkeach" else "_link1")

stopifnot(
  "max_gfp_copies must be at least 1" = params$max_gfp_copies >= 1,
  "linker_between_copies must be TRUE or FALSE" =
    is.logical(params$linker_between_copies) &&
      !is.na(params$linker_between_copies),
  "gfp_copies must be strictly increasing" = all(diff(gfp_copies) > 0),
  "gfp_copies must be a uniform ladder"    =
    length(unique(diff(gfp_copies))) == 1
)
cat("lfc_cutoff =", lfc_cutoff, "| padj_cutoff =", padj_cutoff, "\n")
cat("eGFP copies:", paste(gfp_copies, collapse = ", "),
    "| linker_between_copies =", params$linker_between_copies,
    "| ladder_tag =", ladder_tag, "\n")
```

# 1. Import and Verify the Parts

```{r read_parts}
parts_xlsx <- here("accessories", "cds seq.xlsx")
stopifnot("accessories/cds seq.xlsx not found" = file.exists(parts_xlsx))

parts_tbl <- read_excel(parts_xlsx)
names(parts_tbl)[1] <- "construct"

parts <- parts_tbl %>%
  filter(!is.na(construct), !is.na(cds)) %>%
  transmute(part = tolower(str_trim(construct)),
            seq  = toupper(gsub("\\s", "", cds)))
stopifnot("Duplicate part names in cds seq.xlsx" = !any(duplicated(parts$part)))
pseq <- setNames(parts$seq, parts$part)

needed <- c("smbit n", "p2a", "flag3x", "egfp", "waldo linker")
stopifnot(
  "A required part is missing from cds seq.xlsx" = all(needed %in% names(pseq)),
  "A part contains non-ACGT characters" = all(!grepl("[^ACGT]", pseq[needed])),
  "A part is not divisible by 3" = all(nchar(pseq[needed]) %% 3 == 0)
)

smbit_n <- pseq[["smbit n"]]
p2a     <- pseq[["p2a"]]
flag3x  <- pseq[["flag3x"]]
egfp    <- pseq[["egfp"]]
waldo   <- pseq[["waldo linker"]]

SMBIT_AA  <- "VTGYRLFEEIL"
P2A_AA    <- "ATNFSLLKQAGDVEENPGP"
FLAG_AA   <- "DYKDDDDK"
FLAG3X_AA <- "DYKDHDGDYKDHDIDYKDDDDK"
WALDO_AA  <- "GSAGSAAGSGEF"

aa_of <- function(s) as.character(translate(DNAString(s)))
rc_aa <- function(s) as.character(translate(reverseComplement(DNAString(s))))

flag1x  <- substr(flag3x, 43, 66)
EGFP_AA <- aa_of(egfp)

stopifnot(
  "smBit n does not encode Met + the SmBiT peptide" =
    aa_of(smbit_n) == paste0("M", SMBIT_AA),
  "p2a does not encode the expected 19-aa P2A peptide" = aa_of(p2a) == P2A_AA,
  "flag3x does not encode the canonical 3xFLAG peptide" = aa_of(flag3x) == FLAG3X_AA,
  "1xFLAG is not the 24 nt C-terminal repeat of flag3x" =
    nchar(flag1x) == 24 && endsWith(flag3x, flag1x),
  "1xFLAG does not encode the DYKDDDDK epitope" = aa_of(flag1x) == FLAG_AA,
  "egfp is not 723 nt"           = nchar(egfp) == 723,
  "egfp does not start with ATG" = substr(egfp, 1, 3) == "ATG",
  # The GFP chromophore. avGFP numbers it T65-Y66-G67, but eGFP carries an extra
  # Val at position 2, so it sits at 66-68 here. The position and context matter:
  # TYG also occurs at residue 39, so a motif-presence check would pass on a
  # sequence with no chromophore in place.
  "egfp protein does not carry the TYG chromophore at residues 66-68" =
    substr(EGFP_AA, 66, 68) == "TYG",
  "egfp chromophore is not in the expected LTYGVQCF context" =
    substr(EGFP_AA, 65, 72) == "LTYGVQCF",
  "waldo linker is not 36 nt"    = nchar(waldo) == 36,
  "waldo linker is not in frame" = nchar(waldo) %% 3 == 0,
  "waldo linker does not encode GSAGSAAGSGEF" = aa_of(waldo) == WALDO_AA,
  # The EcoRI site must be in frame at the linker's 3' end, or the Glu-Phe it
  # encodes would not be the two residues the design expects.
  "waldo linker does not end with an in-frame GAATTC EcoRI site" =
    endsWith(waldo, "GAATTC") && (nchar(waldo) - 6) %% 3 == 0
)

# A sequence can be in frame, the right length, and still be backwards, so each
# orientation check is paired with the assertion that the reverse complement
# does NOT encode the same peptide.
stopifnot(
  "Both orientations encode SmBiT: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(smbit_n) != paste0("M", SMBIT_AA),
  "Both orientations encode P2A: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(p2a) != P2A_AA,
  "Both orientations encode FLAG: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(flag1x) != FLAG_AA,
  "Both orientations encode eGFP: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(egfp) != EGFP_AA,
  "Both orientations encode the Waldo linker: the check is not discriminative" =
    rc_aa(waldo) != WALDO_AA
)

stopifnot("A part carries a stop codon" =
            !any(map_lgl(list(smbit_n, p2a, flag1x, egfp, waldo),
                         ~ any(codon_split(.x) %in% STOP_CODONS))))

cat("Parts verified:\n")
for (p in list(c("SmBiT (ATG + 11 aa)", smbit_n), c("P2A", p2a),
               c("FLAG (1x)", flag1x), c("Waldo linker", waldo),
               c("eGFP", egfp))) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-20s %3d nt (%3d codons)  GC %.1f%%  GC3 %.1f%%\n",
              p[1], nchar(p[2]), nchar(p[2]) %/% 3,
              gc_pct_of(p[2]), compute_gc3_pct(p[2])))
}
```

# 2. Build the Ladder

The backbone is `06_`'s SmBiT-P2A-FLAG, unchanged. The Waldo linker joins it to
eGFP, which is then appended as **exact tandem copies** of the supplied 723 nt,
keeping each copy's own `ATG`. Under the default (`linker_between_copies =
FALSE`) the copies after the first are fused directly, so those junctions read
`...MDELYKGT | M VSKGEE...` with an internal Met; under `TRUE` every junction
carries a linker instead. That differs from `05_`, which repeats a short epitope;
here the repeat unit is a whole protein.

```{r build_ladder}
backbone <- paste0(smbit_n, p2a, flag1x)
stopifnot("Backbone is not the 06_ SmBiT-P2A-FLAG construct" =
            nchar(backbone) == nchar(smbit_n) + nchar(p2a) + nchar(flag1x),
          "Backbone protein does not end with the FLAG epitope" =
            endsWith(aa_of(backbone), FLAG_AA))

# The repeat unit: linker + eGFP when every copy gets one, eGFP alone otherwise
# (in which case a single linker is placed once, before the first copy).
unit     <- if (params$linker_between_copies) paste0(waldo, egfp) else egfp
lead_in  <- if (params$linker_between_copies) "" else waldo
step_nt  <- nchar(unit)

build_rung <- function(n) {
  if (n == 0) backbone else paste0(backbone, lead_in, strrep(unit, n))
}
constructs <- map(gfp_copies, build_rung)
names(constructs) <- ifelse(
  gfp_copies == 0, "SmBiT-P2A-FLAG",
  sprintf("SmBiT-P2A-FLAG-link-%dxeGFP", gfp_copies))

cat("Repeat unit:", step_nt, "nt",
    if (params$linker_between_copies) "(linker + eGFP)" else "(eGFP only)",
    "| lead-in:", nchar(lead_in), "nt\n")

cat("Assembled ORF validation:\n")
iwalk(constructs, ~ check_orf(.x, .y))

walk2(constructs, gfp_copies, function(cs, n) {
  aa <- aa_of(cs)
  stopifnot(
    "Construct length is not backbone + lead-in + n * unit" =
      nchar(cs) == nchar(backbone) +
        (if (n == 0) 0 else nchar(lead_in)) + n * step_nt,
    "Construct does not start with the backbone" = startsWith(cs, backbone),
    # One linker per eGFP copy under TRUE, exactly one under FALSE, none at 0.
    "Waldo linker count does not match the design" =
      str_count(cs, fixed(waldo)) ==
        (if (n == 0) 0 else if (params$linker_between_copies) n else 1),
    # The linker must sit immediately after the FLAG tag in both arrangements,
    # which is the placement that was actually asked for.
    "Linker does not immediately follow the FLAG tag" =
      (n == 0) || startsWith(cs, paste0(backbone, waldo)),
    # The copy count itself, asserted on DNA and on protein. If strrep were
    # given the wrong n, or a copy were truncated, this is what fires.
    "eGFP DNA does not appear exactly n times" =
      (if (n == 0) !str_detect(cs, fixed(egfp))
       else length(gregexpr(egfp, cs, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]) == n),
    "eGFP protein does not appear exactly n times" =
      (if (n == 0) !str_detect(aa, fixed(EGFP_AA))
       else length(gregexpr(EGFP_AA, aa, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]) == n),
    "P2A peptide not found exactly once" =
      length(gregexpr(P2A_AA, aa, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]) == 1,
    "Construct protein does not start with Met + SmBiT" =
      startsWith(aa, paste0("M", SMBIT_AA)),
    "Construct protein does not end where it should" =
      endsWith(aa, if (n == 0) FLAG_AA else EGFP_AA)
  )
})
cat("All", length(constructs), "constructs: length additive, exact copy counts,",
    "single in-frame P2A\n")

# The rungs above 0 must be an exactly uniform ladder, which is the property that
# makes this a length series rather than four unrelated constructs.
len <- map_int(constructs, nchar)
gfp_len <- len[gfp_copies > 0]
stopifnot("eGFP rungs are not spaced by exactly one repeat unit" =
            length(unique(diff(gfp_len))) == 1 &&
            unique(diff(gfp_len)) == step_nt)
cat("Rung spacing:", unique(diff(gfp_len)), "nt (one repeat unit)\n")

# Internal EcoRI sites, which the Waldo linker introduces by design. Reported
# rather than asserted away: a property of the linker, not a defect, but it has
# to be visible before anyone picks cloning enzymes.
ecori <- map_int(constructs, ~ str_count(.x, fixed("GAATTC")))
stopifnot(
  "EcoRI site count does not match the linker count" =
    all(ecori == map_int(constructs, ~ str_count(.x, fixed(waldo)))),
  # Discriminative: the 0-copy rung has no linker, so it must have no site.
  "The linker-free rung carries an EcoRI site" = ecori[gfp_copies == 0] == 0
)
cat("Internal EcoRI sites per rung:", paste(ecori, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# No construct may carry a stop codon: the metrics basis is stop-free, but each
# plasmid still needs one appended.
iwalk(constructs, function(cs, nm) {
  stopifnot("Assembled construct unexpectedly carries a terminal stop" =
              !tail(codon_split(cs), 1) %in% STOP_CODONS)
})
cat("No construct carries a stop codon; add one per plasmid (+3 nt not counted)\n")
```

Tandem identical sequence is the construction risk, so it is measured rather than
mentioned. The longest exact internal repeat is reported per construct.

```{r repeat_risk}
rep_tbl <- tibble(
  construct   = names(constructs),
  gfp_copies  = gfp_copies,
  nt          = len,
  # With n exact tandem copies of the repeat unit, the longest repeated block is
  # (n - 1) * unit: the first n-1 copies recur as the last n-1 copies. This
  # holds under both linker arrangements, since the unit is what repeats.
  longest_exact_repeat_nt = pmax(0, (gfp_copies - 1)) * step_nt
)
print(rep_tbl)

stopifnot(
  "Repeat length does not match the copy count" =
    all(rep_tbl$longest_exact_repeat_nt ==
          pmax(0, rep_tbl$gfp_copies - 1) * step_nt),
  # Discriminative: the single-copy construct must have NO internal repeat, or
  # the measure is counting something other than the tandem array.
  "The 1x construct should carry no exact internal repeat" =
    rep_tbl$longest_exact_repeat_nt[rep_tbl$gfp_copies == 1] == 0
)

risky <- rep_tbl %>% filter(longest_exact_repeat_nt > 0)
if (nrow(risky)) {
  cat("\nWARNING: tandem identical repeats present. These recombine in E. coli\n")
  cat("and are hard to sequence through. Codon-divergent eGFP copies remove the\n")
  cat("repeat and would let each copy's GC3 be chosen independently.\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(risky))) {
    cat(sprintf("  %-24s %s nt of exactly repeated sequence\n",
                risky$construct[i], fmt_n(risky$longest_exact_repeat_nt[i])))
  }
}
```

```{r construct_table}
ref_df <- tibble(
  reporter   = names(constructs),
  gfp_copies = gfp_copies,
  cds_length = len,
  gc_pct     = map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc_pct),
  gc3_pct    = map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc3_pct)
)

stopifnot(
  "Reporter GC% out of range"  = all(ref_df$gc_pct  >= 0 & ref_df$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "Reporter GC3% out of range" = all(ref_df$gc3_pct >= 0 & ref_df$gc3_pct <= 100)
)
print(ref_df %>% mutate(across(c(gc_pct, gc3_pct), ~ round(.x, 1))))

# A ladder is ordinal, so the copies get a single-hue ramp rather than
# categorical colours. Dark blue here, against 05_'s reddish-purple ladder, so
# the two ladders are not confusable. Both avoid the density-curve hues
# (grey70 / #E69F00) and the reserved factor hues (#E69F00 eIF3d, #56B4E9 eIF3e).
ref_plot_df <- ref_df %>%
  mutate(color    = colorRampPalette(c("#A6CEE3", "#0072B2", "#03314D"))(n()),
         linetype = "solid",
         reporter = factor(reporter, levels = reporter))
```

# 3. MDA-MB-231 Background and Gene Set

```{r load_promotes}
te_hyp <- read_csv(
  here("output", "translation_categories_si3d_vs_sictrl_hypoxia_1hr.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# Direction check. These files hold the sictrl_vs_si3d coefficient despite the
# filename stating the ratio the other way round, so positive te_lfc = eIF3d
# promotes. EIF3D's own rna_lfc must be strongly positive because the siRNA
# depletes its target.
eif3d_rna <- te_hyp %>% filter(symbol == "EIF3D") %>% pull(rna_lfc)
stopifnot("EIF3D rna_lfc is not strongly positive: contrast direction may be flipped" =
            length(eif3d_rna) == 1 && eif3d_rna > 2)
cat("Direction check - EIF3D rna_lfc:", round(eif3d_rna, 2), "\n")

promotes <- te_hyp %>%
  filter(te_lfc > lfc_cutoff, te_padj < padj_cutoff) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))
stopifnot("Expected 1604 eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes" = nrow(promotes) == 1604)
cat("eIF3d hypoxia-promoted genes:", nrow(promotes), "\n")
```

```{r transcripts}
fm <- readRDS(here("output", "predictive_modeling",
                   "feature_matrix_external_stability.rds"))
tx_all      <- fm %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)
tx_promotes <- tx_all %>% filter(gene_id_clean %in% promotes$gene_id_clean)

missing_gene_ids <- promotes$gene_id_clean[
  !promotes$gene_id_clean %in% tx_all$gene_id_clean]

tx_map <- read_tsv(
  here("accessories", "human", "tx2gene_hs_dm_v49_r111.tsv.gz"),
  col_names = c("transcript_id", "gene_id"), col_types = "cc") %>%
  filter(str_starts(transcript_id, "ENST")) %>%
  transmute(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", transcript_id),
            gene_id_clean       = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id))

hyp_samples <- c("NM2025_0094", "NM2025_0095", "NM2025_0096")
hyp_files   <- setNames(
  file.path(here("2025_MDAcells_riboseq", "salmon"), hyp_samples, "quant.sf.gz"),
  hyp_samples)
stopifnot("Hypoxia siCTRL quant files missing" = all(file.exists(hyp_files)))

extra_tx_df <- map_dfr(names(hyp_files), function(s) {
  read_tsv(hyp_files[[s]], col_types = "cdddd",
           col_names = c("Name", "Length", "EffectiveLength", "TPM", "NumReads"),
           skip = 1) %>% dplyr::select(Name, TPM)
}) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>% summarise(mean_tpm = mean(TPM), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(transcript_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", Name)) %>%
  inner_join(tx_map, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>%
  filter(gene_id_clean %in% missing_gene_ids, mean_tpm > 0) %>%
  group_by(gene_id_clean) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(mean_tpm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(promotes %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, symbol) %>% distinct(),
            by = "gene_id_clean") %>%
  dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, symbol)

tx_promotes <- bind_rows(tx_promotes, extra_tx_df)
cat("Promoted genes with a transcript:", nrow(tx_promotes), "\n")
```

```{r build_metrics}
metrics_all <- build_cds_metrics(
  here("accessories", "human", "txdb.gencode49.sqlite"))

expressed <- tx_all %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)
promoted <- tx_promotes %>%
  inner_join(metrics_all, by = "transcript_id_clean") %>% filter(cds_length > 0)

cat("Expressed transcriptome - valid CDS:", nrow(expressed), "\n")
cat("eIF3d promoted        - valid CDS:", nrow(promoted), "\n")

stopifnot(
  "GC% out of range"  = all(expressed$gc_pct  >= 0 & expressed$gc_pct  <= 100),
  "GC3% out of range" = all(expressed$gc3_pct >= 0 & expressed$gc3_pct <= 100),
  "GC3 median not in expected range [40, 65]" =
    between(median(expressed$gc3_pct), 40, 65)
)

actb <- expressed %>% filter(symbol == "ACTB") %>% dplyr::slice(1)
if (nrow(actb) == 1) {
  stopifnot("ACTB CDS GC% outside expected 50-70%" = between(actb$gc_pct, 50, 70))
  cat("ACTB CDS GC%:", round(actb$gc_pct, 2),
      "| GC3%:", round(actb$gc3_pct, 2), "\n")
}
```

# 4. Density Panels

Every legend entry carries the number it stands for: each density curve shows its
group median, each reference line its own value. Units follow the metric, not the
axis - the length axis is drawn in kb because kb ticks are readable, but a
construct is specified in nt, so the labels say nt.

```{r density_setup}
group_cols <- c("All expressed mRNAs"    = "grey70",
                "eIF3d hypoxia promotes" = "#E69F00")

# NanoLuc is not a reference line here. Asserted rather than assumed.
stopifnot(
  "NanoLuc should not be among the plotted reference lines" =
    !any(str_detect(tolower(as.character(ref_plot_df$reporter)), "nanoluc|nluc")),
  "Expected one reference line per rung" =
    nrow(ref_plot_df) == length(gfp_copies)
)
cat("Reference lines plotted:",
    paste(as.character(ref_plot_df$reporter), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r panel_length, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_len <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "cds_length",
  xlab    = "CDS length (kb)",
  title   = "CDS length, MDA-MB-231, eGFP copy ladder",
  outfile = paste0("cds_reporter_07_density_cds_length_egfp_ladder_",
                   ladder_tag, ".pdf"),
  luc_tbl = ref_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols,
  xscale  = 1000, xmax = 6
)
```

The 0-copy construct is 117 nt and sits on the y axis at this scale. The zoomed
panel is the readable version; the densities are unchanged, only the visible
range differs.

```{r panel_length_zoom, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=5.5}
p_len_zoom <- plot_density_luc(
  expressed, promoted, "cds_length",
  xlab    = "CDS length (kb)",
  # Same title as the wide panel: the zoom is a view of the same data, and the
  # axis shows the range. The filename carries the distinction.
  title   = "CDS length, MDA-MB-231, eGFP copy ladder",
  outfile = paste0("cds_reporter_07_density_cds_length_egfp_ladder_",
                   ladder_tag, "_zoom3kb.pdf"),
  luc_tbl = ref_plot_df, group_cols = group_cols,
  xscale  = 1000, xmax = 3
)
```

# 5. Percentiles

```{r percentiles}
pct_tbl <- reporter_percentiles(expressed, promoted,
                                ref_df %>% dplyr::select(-gfp_copies))
print(pct_tbl)

stopifnot("Percentiles must lie in [0, 100]" =
            all(pct_tbl$pct_expressed >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_expressed <= 100 &
                pct_tbl$pct_promoted  >= 0 & pct_tbl$pct_promoted  <= 100))

write_csv(pct_tbl,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
               paste0("07_egfp_ladder_percentiles_vs_231_", ladder_tag, ".csv")))
cat("Exported: 07_egfp_ladder_percentiles_vs_231_", ladder_tag, ".csv\n", sep = "")
```

# 6. What the Ladder Holds Still, and What It Does Not

`05_` held GC3 still while total GC drifted. This ladder does the opposite of
that failure mode and a new one of its own: above 1 copy **both** GC and GC3 are
nearly fixed, because the construct is asymptotically just eGFP - but they are
fixed far out on the GC3 tail. Both drifts are reported; neither is assumed.

```{r drift}
gfp_only <- ref_df %>% filter(gfp_copies > 0)

drift <- tibble(
  metric = c("cds_length", "gc_pct", "gc3_pct"),
  range_all = c(diff(range(ref_df$cds_length)), diff(range(ref_df$gc_pct)),
                diff(range(ref_df$gc3_pct))),
  range_gfp_rungs = c(diff(range(gfp_only$cds_length)),
                      diff(range(gfp_only$gc_pct)),
                      diff(range(gfp_only$gc3_pct))),
  gene_iqr = c(IQR(expressed$cds_length), IQR(expressed$gc_pct),
               IQR(expressed$gc3_pct))
) %>%
  mutate(pct_of_iqr_all  = round(100 * range_all / gene_iqr, 1),
         pct_of_iqr_gfp  = round(100 * range_gfp_rungs / gene_iqr, 1),
         across(c(range_all, range_gfp_rungs, gene_iqr), ~ round(.x, 1)))
print(drift)

len_share <- drift$pct_of_iqr_gfp[drift$metric == "cds_length"]
gc3_share <- drift$pct_of_iqr_gfp[drift$metric == "gc3_pct"]
gc_share  <- drift$pct_of_iqr_gfp[drift$metric == "gc_pct"]

stopifnot(
  # The property that makes this a length series: across the eGFP rungs, length
  # must move far more than composition does, in distribution units.
  "Across the eGFP rungs, length does not dominate composition" =
    len_share > 5 * max(gc3_share, gc_share)
)
cat(sprintf("\nAcross the eGFP rungs: length moves %.1f%% of the expressed IQR,\n",
            len_share))
cat(sprintf("GC %.1f%% and GC3 %.1f%%. Length dominates by %.0fx.\n",
            gc_share, gc3_share, len_share / max(gc3_share, gc_share)))

# The level, not the drift, is the problem. Reported as a warning rather than an
# assertion, because it is a property of eGFP, not a defect in the ladder.
gc3_pcts <- pct_tbl %>% filter(metric == "gc3_pct")
cat("\nWARNING: the ladder is composition-stable but sits on the GC3 tail.\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gc3_pcts))) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-24s GC3 %5.1f%%  = %5.1f pct of expressed, %5.1f pct of promoted\n",
              gc3_pcts$reporter[i], gc3_pcts$reporter_value[i],
              gc3_pcts$pct_expressed[i], gc3_pcts$pct_promoted[i]))
}
cat("A codon-shuffled eGFP would keep the lengths and move GC3 to any target.\n")

write_csv(drift,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
               paste0("07_egfp_ladder_drift_", ladder_tag, ".csv")))
```

```{r export_sequences}
seq_out <- tibble(
  reporter = names(constructs),
  gfp_copies = gfp_copies,
  length_nt_stop_free = len,
  gc_pct   = round(map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc_pct), 3),
  gc3_pct  = round(map_dbl(constructs, orf_gc3_pct), 3),
  longest_exact_repeat_nt = rep_tbl$longest_exact_repeat_nt,
  bases    = unlist(constructs, use.names = FALSE)
)
write_csv(seq_out,
          here("output", "cds_reporter_design",
               paste0("07_egfp_ladder_assembled_sequences_", ladder_tag, ".csv")))
cat("Exported: 07_egfp_ladder_assembled_sequences_", ladder_tag, ".csv and ",
    "07_egfp_ladder_drift_", ladder_tag, ".csv\n", sep = "")
```

# 7. Summary

```{r summary}
cat("=== SmBiT-P2A-FLAG eGFP copy ladder vs MDA-MB-231 ===\n\n")
cat("Backbone: smBit n (ATG + SmBiT) + P2A + 1xFLAG =", nchar(backbone), "nt\n")
cat("Waldo linker (", nchar(waldo), " nt, ", WALDO_AA, ") joins FLAG to eGFP; ",
    if (params$linker_between_copies) "one per copy.\n" else
      "one in total.\n", sep = "")
cat("Each rung appends one exact tandem copy of the", step_nt,
    "nt repeat unit,\nkeeping eGFP's own ATG, so each junction carries an internal Met.\n")
cat("No construct has a stop codon; each plasmid needs one appended.\n\n")

for (i in seq_len(nrow(ref_df))) {
  cat(sprintf("%-24s %d copies  %5d nt (%4d codons)  GC %.1f%%  GC3 %.1f%%\n",
              ref_df$reporter[i], ref_df$gfp_copies[i], ref_df$cds_length[i],
              ref_df$cds_length[i] / 3, ref_df$gc_pct[i], ref_df$gc3_pct[i]))
}

cat(sprintf("\nMDA-MB-231 medians: all expressed %.0f nt / GC %.1f%% / GC3 %.1f%%\n",
            median(expressed$cds_length), median(expressed$gc_pct),
            median(expressed$gc3_pct)))
cat(sprintf("                    promoted      %.0f nt / GC %.1f%% / GC3 %.1f%%\n",
            median(promoted$cds_length), median(promoted$gc_pct),
            median(promoted$gc3_pct)))

cat("\nLength percentiles:\n")
lp <- pct_tbl %>% filter(metric == "cds_length")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(lp))) {
  cat(sprintf("  %-24s %5.0f nt  ->  %5.1f pct expressed, %5.1f pct promoted\n",
              lp$reporter[i], lp$reporter_value[i],
              lp$pct_expressed[i], lp$pct_promoted[i]))
}
```
